description: From putting a pixel on the screen to rendering lit, shaded 3D scenes in the browser: rasterisation algorithms, transformations, viewing, clipping, visibility, shading and a working WebGL pipeline. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer graphics course.
modelledOn: Marschner and Shirley, Fundamentals of Computer Graphics
Hearn, Baker and Carithers, Computer Graphics with OpenGL
Cantor and Jones, WebGL Beginner's Guide
outcomes: Explain raster and vector representations, colour models and the graphics pipeline.
Implement line, circle and polygon rasterisation and filling algorithms and anti-aliasing.
Compose 2D and 3D transformations with homogeneous matrices and quaternions.
Set up cameras, projections and viewports and clip primitives against the view volume.
Resolve visibility with z-buffer and related methods and shade surfaces with Phong and physically based models.
Write WebGL programs with vertex and fragment shaders, buffers, textures and interaction.

units.title: Raster and vector graphics
topics: Images as pixel grids; frame buffers, resolution, colour depth; displays from CRT to OLED
Colour: RGB, CMYK, HSV, gamma; colour perception and dithering
Vector graphics: paths, SVG, Bezier curves; scalable versus raster
The graphics pipeline overview: modelling, transformation, rasterisation, shading, display
Drawing pixels on an HTML canvas; image formats and compression (PNG, JPEG)

units.title: Line, circle and polygon drawing algorithms
topics: DDA and Bresenham line algorithms; symmetry and integer arithmetic
Midpoint circle and ellipse algorithms
Scan-line polygon fill, edge tables, boundary and flood fill
Anti-aliasing: supersampling, Wu's algorithm, coverage
Thick lines, line styles and character rasterisation

units.title: 2D transformations
topics: Translation, rotation, scaling, shear, reflection as matrices; homogeneous coordinates
Composition and order; rotation about an arbitrary point
Window-to-viewport mapping; coordinate systems
Hierarchical modelling: a 2D articulated figure

units.title: 3D transformations and modelling
topics: 3D homogeneous transforms; rotation about arbitrary axes; Euler angles, gimbal lock, quaternions
Scene graphs and model-view hierarchies
Representing surfaces: polygon meshes, normals, indexed triangles; parametric surfaces and subdivision in brief
Loading and displaying an OBJ model

units.title: Viewing and projection
topics: Camera model: eye, look-at, up; the view matrix
Orthographic and perspective projection matrices; field of view, near and far planes
Normalised device coordinates and the viewport transform
Depth precision and the perspective divide

units.title: Clipping and hidden surfaces
topics: Cohen-Sutherland and Liang-Barsky line clipping; Sutherland-Hodgman polygon clipping; clipping in homogeneous space
Back-face culling
Z-buffer algorithm; painter's algorithm; BSP trees; scan-line visibility
Ray casting as an alternative; bounding volumes and spatial subdivision

units.title: Shading and lighting
topics: Light sources: ambient, directional, point, spot; attenuation
Lambertian diffuse, Phong and Blinn-Phong specular; material properties
Flat, Gouraud and Phong shading; vertex normals
Texture mapping, mipmaps, bump and normal mapping; environment maps
Shadows (shadow maps), global illumination and ray tracing in brief; physically based rendering overview

units.title: Introduction to WebGL
topics: WebGL context, buffers, attributes, uniforms; GLSL vertex and fragment shaders
Drawing triangles, applying matrices with a maths library, animation with requestAnimationFrame
Lighting and texturing in shaders; loading textures and models
Mouse and keyboard interaction: orbit camera, picking
Performance on low-end phones; three.js as a higher-level alternative
Project: an interactive 3D scene such as a model of a Ghanaian landmark or a data visualisation

schedule.title: Pixels, colour and vector graphics
schedule.exercise: Short lab report: compute the memory needed for a 1080p frame buffer at three colour depths, convert five colours between RGB and HSV by hand, and explain when SVG beats a bitmap.

tasks.title: Compute frame buffer sizes in megabytes for 640x480 at 8, 16 and 24 bits per pixel and check them against a table of resolutions
Write a program that converts RGB to HSV and applies gamma correction, then verify it against ten known colour values
Evaluate a cubic Bezier curve with de Casteljau subdivision, render it on a canvas, and compare file size with an equivalent raster image

schedule.title: The pipeline and the canvas
schedule.exercise: Draw a labelled diagram of the graphics pipeline for a single triangle and write a half-page comparison of PNG and JPEG for photographs versus diagrams.

tasks.title: Write code that pushes one triangle through modelling, transformation and rasterisation stages, printing the vertex coordinates after each stage
Draw a gradient and a checkerboard pixel by pixel on a canvas, then export it and compare the sizes of PNG and JPEG versions
Implement a run-length encoder for a 256x256 image, measure compression on a flat graphic versus a photograph and explain the difference

schedule.title: Lines, circles and polygon fill
schedule.exercise: Trace the Bresenham algorithm by hand for two lines, then program line, circle and polygon fill routines on a pixel grid.

tasks.title: Implement the DDA line algorithm, draw five lines of different slopes on a pixel grid and compare each with the exact line
Implement the midpoint circle algorithm using only integer arithmetic and verify that all eight symmetric octants line up for radii 5 to 50
Implement scan-line polygon fill with an edge table for a concave polygon and compare it against flood fill on the same shape

schedule.title: Anti-aliasing and text rasterisation
schedule.exercise: Compare aliased and anti-aliased renderings of the same diagonal lines and write up the cost in extra samples per pixel.

tasks.title: Render a diagonal line with and without 4x supersampling on a small grid and count how many pixels change intensity
Implement Wu's line algorithm, render it beside Bresenham's and measure the coverage error against an exact area calculation
Rasterise a letter from a bitmap font at three scales, draw thick dashed lines, and compare jaggedness with and without anti-aliasing

schedule.title: 2D transformations
schedule.exercise: Problem set: write the 3x3 matrices for five transformations, compose them for rotation about a point, and explain why order matters.

tasks.title: Apply translation, rotation and scaling matrices to a triangle with vertices you choose and plot the original and transformed shapes
Compose a matrix that rotates a square 45 degrees about its own centre, then show that reversing the order gives a different result
Build a 2D articulated robot arm with a shoulder, elbow and wrist using nested matrix transforms, and animate it to reach a given point

schedule.title: 3D transforms, scene graphs and meshes
schedule.exercise: Build a small scene graph for a toy truck with wheels, write out its model matrices, and describe how an OBJ file stores a mesh.

tasks.title: Rotate a cube vertex set about the X, Y and Z axes with 4x4 matrices and print the new coordinates for 45 degrees
Build a scene graph for a toy truck whose four wheels spin relative to the body, and print each node's final model matrix
Parse an OBJ file, compute vertex normals by averaging face normals, and report the triangle count and bounding box of the model

schedule.title: Camera and projection
schedule.exercise: Derive the perspective projection matrix for a given field of view and aspect ratio, and track a vertex through to pixel coordinates.

tasks.title: Build a view matrix from eye, look-at and up vectors for a camera at (4,3,5) and transform three scene points into camera space
Construct orthographic and perspective projection matrices for the same view volume and compare how a row of cubes appears in each plot
Project a vertex through the full pipeline to pixel coordinates, then show how the depth value loses precision when the near plane moves closer to zero

schedule.title: Clipping and culling
schedule.exercise: Clip five line segments against a window with both Cohen-Sutherland and Liang-Barsky by hand and compare how many steps each used.

tasks.title: Implement Cohen-Sutherland line clipping against a rectangular window and report the outcode of each endpoint for 20 test lines
Implement Sutherland-Hodgman polygon clipping against a rectangle and test it on a concave polygon that produces degenerate edges
Implement back-face culling for a cube using face normals and the view direction, and verify that exactly half the faces are rejected from any angle

schedule.title: Visibility
schedule.exercise: Write a short comparison of the z-buffer, painter's algorithm and ray casting in memory, speed and failure cases, with a sketch of a cyclic overlap.

tasks.title: Implement a z-buffer for three overlapping triangles and render the result, checking that draw order no longer changes the picture
Show the painter's algorithm failing for three mutually overlapping triangles, then fix it with a BSP split of one polygon
Cast one ray per pixel against a sphere and a plane, add a bounding volume test and measure how many intersection tests it saves

schedule.title: Lighting and shading
schedule.exercise: Compute Lambertian and Blinn-Phong intensities for a point on a sphere by hand, then compare flat, Gouraud and Phong shading renders.

tasks.title: Calculate the intensity at three surface points for a point light with inverse-square attenuation and plot intensity against distance
Implement Lambertian diffuse plus Blinn-Phong specular on a sphere and render it with three different shininess values
Render the same low-polygon sphere with flat, Gouraud and Phong shading and explain why Gouraud misses a highlight inside a triangle

schedule.title: Textures and global effects
schedule.exercise: Write a design note on how you would add textures, shadows and reflections to a market stall scene on a low-end phone.

tasks.title: Map a checkerboard texture onto a quad with bilinear filtering and show the aliasing at a distance, then add a mipmap level and compare
Implement normal mapping on a flat quad by perturbing the lighting normal from a normal map and check it responds to a moving light
Add a hard shadow to a ray-traced scene with two spheres and a plane, then add one mirror reflection bounce and count the extra rays

schedule.title: WebGL basics and shaders
schedule.exercise: Write a vertex and fragment shader pair that draws a coloured, spinning triangle and annotate each line of the GLSL.

tasks.title: Create a WebGL context, upload a triangle's vertex buffer and write a fragment shader that colours it with a per-vertex gradient
Animate a spinning cube with model, view and projection matrices from a maths library driven by requestAnimationFrame
Write a fragment shader implementing Blinn-Phong lighting on a textured model and add a uniform to toggle the texture

schedule.title: Interaction and the 3D project
schedule.exercise: Project plan: a one-page proposal for an interactive 3D scene (landmark or data visualisation) with a frame-rate budget for a low-end phone.

tasks.title: Implement an orbit camera controlled by the mouse that never flips past the poles and test it with a spinning model
Profile a scene of 2,000 cubes, then reduce draw calls with instancing and measure the frame time before and after
Build an interactive 3D bar chart of regional cocoa output with picking, an orbit camera and a frame budget of 30 frames per second
